agent_notes: Hebrew verses 1-2 are the superscription; the KJV counts them as verse 0 and starts its verse 1 at Hebrew verse 3. Shushan Eduth is rendered 'Lily of Testimony' as a literal title; whether it is a tune name, an instrument or a flower-shaped object is uncertain, and the commentaries split (Ibn Ezra: tune from an opening line; Meiri and Metzudat Zion: an instrument shaped like a lily).

agent_notes: Rashi (and Metzudat Zion) read נַעֲלִי as a bolt or lock from מנעול; the standard reading, and mine, is 'sandal'. The gesture of casting the sandal over a place is a claim of ownership, as in Ruth 4:7; I make no claim beyond what the verse says about Edom.

KJV and BBE turn the perfect נָחַנִי into a future ('will lead', 'will be my guide'); ASV and YLT keep the past ('hath led'). I keep the perfect, as the literal layer must. The Targum reads מָצוֹר as the city name Tyre ('to the ruined city of Tyre'); I mention it in the commentary and keep 'fortification'. Rashi, Radak and Meiri do not agree on whether the verse looks back (Meiri, Radak: what God has done) or forward (Rashi: 'who will lead me against Edom's strongholds').

agent_notes: פְּצַמְתָּהּ is a hapax. Rashi glosses it 'you broke it' (שברת אותה); he reports Moshe HaDarshan's 'tearing', argued from the Targum's ופצים at Jer 22:14, and disputes only that proof (for Rashi ופצים there is the fitting of a window frame). Radak and Metzudat Zion give 'splitting open'. I render 'split open', the sense the five versions and Radak share.

agent_notes: BBE renders the verse as a petition for refuge from the bow, reading קֹשֶׁט as קֶשֶׁת; the consonants differ (ט vs ת) and the written text has קֹשֶׁט 'truth'. I follow the written text, noting that the pun with נֵס/הִתְנוֹסֵס gives the 'banner' sense and that an old alternative reading 'flee' (from נוּס) is possible.

The last word is a Ketiv/Qere pair: written ועננו 'and answer us' (followed by ASV and YLT, and glossed so by Radak 'ועננו בתפלה זאת' and Meiri), read וַעֲנֵנִי 'and answer me' (followed by KJV, BBE and Rashi). The literal layer, the dramatic layer and the gloss follow the Qere 'me'; the commentary gives both.

agent_notes: STEPBible glosses מְחֹקְקִי 'commander's staff', the versions 'lawgiver' or 'sceptre'. The participle can be the one who inscribes or decrees, and the word also names the ruler's staff (Gen 49:10, Num 21:18). I render 'my commander's staff' in the literal layer and keep 'lawgiver' in the commentary.
